findings.claim: In January 2021 US Customs detained Uniqlo cotton shirts at Los Angeles under an order targeting Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps cotton, and in May 2021 rejected Uniqlo's protest, finding its evidence that no forced labour was involved insufficient. Fast Retailing said its cotton came from outside China; CBP later withdrew the rulings, saying Uniqlo had withdrawn its protests.

NGOs alleged in French complaints from 2021 and 2023 that Uniqlo France and three other groups sold goods made partly with forced Uyghur labour; the company says there is no forced labour in its supply chains. No investigation was opened: prosecutors and a judge declined jurisdiction, upheld on appeal in February 2025, and a new complaint was announced.

About 2,000 workers lost their jobs when Indonesian supplier Jaba Garmindo went bankrupt in 2015; Clean Clothes Campaign says about $5.5 million in severance is unpaid and Fast Retailing refuses to contribute. The Fair Labor Association found no violation by Fast Retailing and recommended voluntary relief; the company funded an ILO project in Indonesia instead, and the FLA closed the case in 2023.

Tokyo courts dismissed Fast Retailing and Uniqlo's ¥220 million libel suit against publisher Bungeishunju in October 2013 and on appeal in March 2014, finding reporting on long hours in Japanese stores true in its important parts. The publisher says the outcome was confirmed by the Supreme Court; the rulings are over ten years old.

In October 2022 South Korea's Fair Trade Commission imposed a provisional fine of 153 million won on FRL Korea, Uniqlo's Korean operator, for overstating antibacterial and deodorising claims for AIRism and DRY-EX garments in ads run from 2018 to 2020.

Fast Retailing reports that by FY2024 it had cut emissions from its stores and main offices by 83.3% and from its supply chain by 18.6% against FY2019, with 84.7% renewable electricity. Its 2030 supply-chain target was raised from 20% to 30% in November 2025; the figures are self-reported.

Under agreements announced by Kyoto University in 2020, Yanai personally funds cancer immunology and iPS cell research there, including ¥4.5 billion to the iPS Cell Research Foundation paid at ¥500 million a year from FY2021. A clinical iPS cell production site named after him opened in Osaka in June 2025.

social.reason: Documented company-level labour problems. US Customs blocked Uniqlo shirts in 2021, finding the company had not shown its cotton was free of Xinjiang forced labour. Workers of a bankrupt Indonesian supplier say $5.5 million in severance is unpaid; a monitor found no violation by Fast Retailing. Japanese courts found reporting on long store hours true in key parts (2013-2014). French forced-labour complaints remain allegations.

legal.reason: Regulatory record at company level: a provisional fine of 153 million won on Uniqlo's Korean operator for misleading garment ads (2022) and the 2021 US customs detention of Uniqlo shirts. Fast Retailing also lost a libel suit it brought over labour reporting. No personal legal record for Tadashi Yanai was found.

unresolved.reason: No pending case or investigation was found. Concerns raised by NGOs remain open: a campaign for unpaid severance at a former Indonesian supplier, which Fast Retailing declines to pay, and forced-labour complaints in France that courts declined to investigate, with a new filing announced. Nothing personal is pending.

proposal.counterweights: Tadashi Yanai personally funds research at Kyoto University, including ¥4.5 billion to its iPS cell foundation in yearly instalments since 2021. Fast Retailing reports an 18.6% cut in supply-chain emissions and 83.3% in its own operations by FY2024 against 2019 (self-reported).
proposal.rationale: Social stays 2, now documented: no forced-labour finding against Uniqlo itself (CBP found its evidence insufficient, not forced labour proven), so 3 is not supported. Legal 0 to 1: a Korean regulatory fine on a 51%-owned operator plus the CBP detention fit level 1. Unresolved 0 to 1: open NGO-raised concerns, but no pending case. Ecology and politics not proposed: the emissions disclosure is self-reported and no political activity was checked; ecology stays 3.
